summary: The Puppy Protection Act of 2025 amends the Animal Welfare Act to require dog dealers to meet detailed new standards including solid-floor unstacked enclosures with minimum space per dog, twice-daily feeding, continuous clean water, daily outdoor exercise, 30 minutes of daily socialization, annual vet exams plus vaccinations and parasite prevention, pre-breeding health screenings with limits on litters and breeding ages by size, and efforts to rehome retired breeding dogs.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Animal Welfare Act to impose new regulatory standards on private dog dealers. It does not authorize or appropriate any federal funds, expand government programs, or affect federal budgets in any direct way. Any minor administrative costs for issuing regulations would be negligible and incidental.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses standards for veterinary care of dogs held by dealers, but this is strictly animal welfare regulation and has no bearing on human healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms, gun ownership, or regulations.
No provisions relate to immigration, borders, or foreign nationals.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military or defense spending.
The bill focuses narrowly on humane treatment standards for dogs in commercial breeding facilities and does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or conservation.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement or decriminalization.

The bill adds regulatory requirements under the Animal Welfare Act, which already includes civil and criminal penalties for violations, but it does not address sentencing reform, policing practices, or broader criminal justice policy.
No provisions relate to trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export policy.
No provisions relate to deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions relate to foreign aid.
No provisions relate to voting access or election integrity.
No provisions relate to technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions relate to labor rights, unions, or employment regulations.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
